findings.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug logging left at Error level (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579) fires on every batch including the empty terminal batch and dumps full ID lists, flooding logs and error-rate alerts every cleanup cycle.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker cut from 10m to 1m while the per-run timeout stays 9m, so all eight cleanup jobs (dashboard versions, snapshots, query history, etc.) run nearly back-to-back on every HA replica, multiplying DB load ~10x for changes unrelated to annotations.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so a configured batch size above 65535 exceeds the Postgres/MySQL placeholder limit and every run errors out without deleting anything (old subquery DELETE had no such limit).

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — Inline SQLite ID list is built by repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is O(n^2) in copying and allocation (GBs copied per batch at 32k IDs).

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Test named "running the max count delete again" now seeds a fresh dataset instead of re-running on the prior subtest's state, so it no longer verifies that a second run is idempotent.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered only after seeding and the require-based asserts, so an early failure leaves rows with fixed explicit IDs 1..N behind, and later subtests then fail on duplicate keys.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug tracing left in at Error level in every batch (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579), including the full ID slice (up to batch size) and err values that are always nil; successful cleanups now produce Error logs on every run, even when nothing is deleted (tag cleanup always logs "count 0"), which floods error logs and trips error-based alerting.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker drops from 10m to 1m for all eight cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, short URLs, query history, and so on), not only annotations. That is 10x the DB cleanup load, and the 9-minute per-run timeout at line 89, sized to fit the 10m interval, no longer matches.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID. With cleanupjob_batchsize above 65535, Postgres (65535 bind-parameter limit) and MySQL prepared statements (65535 placeholders) fail every batch, so cleanup never makes progress. The old subquery DELETE used no parameters and worked with any batch size.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The SQLite inline-vs-placeholder choice checks the configured batch size, not len(ids). With a non-positive batch size, SQLite's LIMIT -1 returns every matching ID and they all get bound as placeholders, so the delete can go over SQLite's variable limit and fail.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Each subtest now reseeds its own fresh data, so the "running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations" case never runs cleanup a second time on already-cleaned data and no longer tests idempotency.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered after createTestAnnotations and the require-based count assertions. If any of those fail, rows with explicit IDs 1..N stay in the shared DB and later subtests fail with duplicate primary-key errors, which hides the original failure.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Leftover debug logging at Error level (6 call sites, lines 534-579) fires on every batch including zero-row no-op batches and dumps the full ids slice (up to batch size) into logs, so healthy cleanup looks like errors every minute.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker is hardcoded to 1m with no explanation or config, and is no longer tied to the 9m job timeout at line 89, which only made sense next to the old 10m interval.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:548 — Three nearly identical closures (build cond, fetchIDs, log, deleteByIDs, log) are copy-pasted across the MaxAge, MaxCount and orphan-tag paths (528-581) and should be one helper that takes table and condition.
pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — Meaningless names `x, y` for deleteByIDs' (affected, err) results hurt readability, and the pattern is repeated at 556 and 578.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — The `"err", err` log field is always nil because the non-nil case already returned at line 532, so it is a dead field (same at 554 and 576).

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:584 — fetchIDs takes a raw SQL `condition` string that actually carries ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET clauses, so the name is misleading and the API is stringly typed (callers at 529, 549, 571).
pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:585 — fetchIDs builds the SQL string before checking for an empty condition; the guard should come first so the reader is not misled.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:605 — Magic constant 999 and its "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" comment only describe SQLite before 3.32, while the new test targets the 32767 limit of newer versions, so comment and test disagree.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The generic deleteByIDs helper picks its inline-vs-placeholder branch from annotation-specific r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize instead of len(ids), which couples it to cleanup config rather than the actual parameter count.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — The IN-list is built by repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation (quadratic, hard to read) where strings.Join over formatted ids would be clearer.
pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:13 — The storage layer now imports sqlstore/migrator just to compare DB type, adding a dependency on the migration package for a dialect check.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:274 — The batched InsertMulti loop (batchsize := 500) is duplicated verbatim for annotations and annotation tags (274 and 284), so it should be a small generic helper or shared constant.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cutting the ticker from 10m to 1m makes all eight cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history, tmp files) run 10x as often on every install, and because the 9m per-run timeout is unchanged, a heavy run can now go straight into the next one with no idle gap, so DB load never lets up.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Leftover debug logging at Error level writes the full `ids` slice (up to batch-size elements) plus two lines per batch at 534/537, 554/557, 576/579, including the final empty batch, so every cleanup run floods logs and allocates large formatted strings, now once a minute.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — The SQLite IN-list is built by repeated `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`, which copies the whole string on every append and is O(n^2) (about 32k IDs means gigabytes of copying per batch); use strings.Builder or strings.Join.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — Each batch now takes two separate sessions and round-trips (SELECT ids, then DELETE ... IN (...)) instead of one statement, which doubles per-batch latency and connection churn at the default small batch size.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug logging left at Error level (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579) fires on every batch, including successful and empty terminal batches with err=nil, so every instance emits error logs every cycle, which floods logs and trips error-rate alerts.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:554 — Per-batch log lines include the full `ids` slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries, e.g. 32767), producing unbounded log lines that can exceed log shipper limits and bloat storage.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker cut from 10m to 1m while the per-run timeout stays 9m (line 89), so with any backlog cleanup runs back-to-back nearly nonstop, and all eight jobs run 10x more often on every HA instance (clean() takes no server lock), which adds DB load and the delete contention this PR is meant to reduce.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so on MySQL/Postgres a configured batch size above 65535 makes every delete fail, and cleanup errors out permanently, where the old single-statement DELETE had no parameter limit.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:610 — The SQLite inline-ID path builds the IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is O(n^2) (several GB of copying at 32767 IDs per batch) and can burn CPU and use up the cleanup timeout.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered only after createTestAnnotations and the count asserts, so a failure there leaks rows into the shared DB and the fixed IDs 1..N then cause PK collisions in every later subtest.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:277 — require.NoError is called inside the WithDbSession closures and the closures always return nil, so the outer require.NoError(err) checks at lines 281 and 291 can never fail.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Each subtest now seeds fresh data, so "running the max count delete again" no longer re-runs cleanup on already-cleaned state and only checks the exactly-at-MaxCount case.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:98 — The test name cites SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766), but the code switches at 999 (xorm_store.go:607), and no case tests batch size 999 or 1000, so a wrong threshold below 32767 would go unnoticed.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:99 — The 40003-row case inserts about 120k rows and runs the O(n^2) fmt.Sprintf ID-string build in the SQLite path, which makes the suite much slower for one branch check.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:643 — The new untilDoneOrCancelled, fetchIDs and deleteByIDs helpers have no tests for context cancellation (partial count plus ctx.Err), an error mid-batch, or the empty-condition guard.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:569 — The rewritten orphaned-tag cleanup is only tested with tags orphaned in the same run (tags always equal 2x annotations), never with pre-existing orphans or a mixed state.
pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — The ticker drops from 10m to 1m with no test, and the 9m per-run timeout is now longer than the tick interval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug logging left at Error level (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579) fires on every batch including the empty terminal batch and dumps full ID lists, flooding logs and error-rate alerts every cleanup cycle.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker cut from 10m to 1m while the per-run timeout stays 9m, so all eight cleanup jobs (dashboard versions, snapshots, query history, etc.) run nearly back-to-back on every HA replica, multiplying DB load ~10x for changes unrelated to annotations.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so a configured batch size above 65535 exceeds the Postgres/MySQL placeholder limit and every run errors out without deleting anything (old subquery DELETE had no such limit).

adjudication.rationale: The new cleanup path fetches up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` IDs and then deletes via `DELETE ... WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` in `deleteByIDs` (non-SQLite, or SQLite with batch size <= 999). This binds one parameter per ID (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)` and `args = asAny(ids)`), so if `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured very large, the generated statement can exceed DB parameter/placeholder limits (e.g., Postgres’ 65535). The prior implementation used a subquery delete with `LIMIT` and did not create O(batch size) bound parameters, so this risk is introduced by the diff and would cause the job to error before deleting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — Inline SQLite ID list is built by repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is O(n^2) in copying and allocation (GBs copied per batch at 32k IDs).

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, for SQLite when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the code builds the `IN (...)` list by repeatedly reassigning `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop over `ids[1:]`. This is repeated string concatenation with growing strings, which is O(n^2) in time/copying and can cause large allocations for large batches (e.g., the test sets batch size 32767). It’s a real, diff-grounded performance concern but not inherently a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Test named "running the max count delete again" now seeds a fresh dataset instead of re-running on the prior subtest's state, so it no longer verifies that a second run is idempotent.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each subtest now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` inside `t.Run` and registers a per-subtest `t.Cleanup` that deletes from `annotation`/`annotation_tag`. This isolates state between subtests. As a result, the case named "running the max count delete again..." no longer re-runs cleanup on the dataset produced by the prior "should only keep three annotations" subtest; it instead runs once on a freshly seeded dataset (9 annotations). That weakens/changes the intent of verifying idempotency across two runs, but it’s a test coverage issue rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered only after seeding and the require-based asserts, so an early failure leaves rows with fixed explicit IDs 1..N behind, and later subtests then fail on duplicate keys.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each subtest seeds rows via `createTestAnnotations` (which now sets explicit `ID: int64(i+1)` for every inserted annotation) and then runs `assertAnnotationCount` / `assertAnnotationTagCount` **before** registering the subtest `t.Cleanup` that deletes from `annotation` and `annotation_tag`. Since `fakeSQL := db.InitTestDB(t)` is created once and shared across subtests, any early failure/panic/`require.*` failure during seeding or the pre-cleanup asserts will prevent the cleanup from being registered, leaving rows with fixed IDs behind and causing later subtests to hit duplicate key conflicts when inserting IDs 1..N again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID. With cleanupjob_batchsize above 65535, Postgres (65535 bind-parameter limit) and MySQL prepared statements (65535 placeholders) fail every batch, so cleanup never makes progress. The old subquery DELETE used no parameters and worked with any batch size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces single-statement DELETE subqueries with a two-step fetchIDs + deleteByIDs loop. In deleteByIDs(), the non-SQLite branch builds an `IN (?, ?, ... )` list with one placeholder per ID (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`), and `ids` comes from `fetchIDs()` limited only by `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`. There is no cap/guard on batch size for non-SQLite, so if `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured very large, each batch can generate tens of thousands of bind parameters and fail at the driver/DB limit, preventing cleanup progress. This risk is introduced by the new implementation; the old subquery DELETE path didn’t create a placeholder per ID.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The SQLite inline-vs-placeholder choice checks the configured batch size, not len(ids). With a non-positive batch size, SQLite's LIMIT -1 returns every matching ID and they all get bound as placeholders, so the delete can go over SQLite's variable limit and fail.

adjudication.rationale: In deleteByIDs(), the SQLite parameter-limit workaround is gated on r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999, not on the actual number of IDs being deleted (len(ids)). The number of placeholders is built from len(ids) ("?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)), so if fetchIDs() ever returns >999 IDs while AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is <=999 (e.g., due to a non-positive/misconfigured batch size leading to an unbounded/ineffective LIMIT in the SELECT condition), the code will choose the placeholder path and can exceed SQLite's variable limit and fail. This risk is introduced by the new fetch-IDs-then-delete-by-IN-list approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Each subtest now reseeds its own fresh data, so the "running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations" case never runs cleanup a second time on already-cleaned data and no longer tests idempotency.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each `t.Run` subtest now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` before running `cleaner.Run(...)` and registers a cleanup that deletes the tables afterward. This means the case named "running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations" no longer runs cleanup a second time on already-cleaned data; it runs on freshly inserted 9 annotations with `MaxCount=3`, which should delete 6, yet the test still expects `affectedAnnotations: 0`. So the subtest no longer tests idempotency and appears logically incorrect given the new per-subtest reseeding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered after createTestAnnotations and the require-based count assertions. If any of those fail, rows with explicit IDs 1..N stay in the shared DB and later subtests fail with duplicate primary-key errors, which hides the original failure.

adjudication.rationale: In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, each subtest calls createTestAnnotations(...) and then require/assert-based count checks *before* registering t.Cleanup. Since fakeSQL is initialized once outside the subtests and createTestAnnotations now assigns explicit IDs (ID: int64(i+1)), if createTestAnnotations or the pre-cleanup assertions fail, the subtest can abort without having registered the cleanup that deletes from annotation/annotation_tag. Those rows can remain in the shared test DB and cause later subtests to hit duplicate primary-key errors, masking the original failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Leftover debug logging at Error level (6 call sites, lines 534-579) fires on every batch including zero-row no-op batches and dumps the full ids slice (up to batch size) into logs, so healthy cleanup looks like errors every minute.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the cleanup batch loops in `xorm_store.go` (e.g., in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`) that log on every batch, including the terminal no-op batch where `ids` is empty and `affected` becomes 0. These logs also include the full `ids` slice (`"ids", ids`), which could be large up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`. This is noisy/misleading (Error level for normal operation) and potentially heavy, but it’s not a functional correctness defect in the cleanup logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker is hardcoded to 1m with no explanation or config, and is no longer tied to the 9m job timeout at line 89, which only made sense next to the old 10m interval.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the cleanup loop ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`) with no accompanying comment or configuration knob. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/operability concern (more frequent runs, unclear rationale). The finding’s additional claim about being “no longer tied to the 9m job timeout at line 89” is not directly verifiable from the provided diff context, so it can’t be confirmed as a correctness defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:548 — Three nearly identical closures (build cond, fetchIDs, log, deleteByIDs, log) are copy-pasted across the MaxAge, MaxCount and orphan-tag paths (528-581) and should be one helper that takes table and condition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds three very similar `untilDoneOrCancelled` batch closures: one for MaxAge cleanup (around the new code that builds `cond`, calls `r.fetchIDs("annotation", cond)`, logs, then `r.deleteByIDs("annotation", ids)`), one for MaxCount cleanup (same pattern with different `cond`), and one for orphaned tag cleanup (same pattern on `annotation_tag`). This is visible copy/paste duplication in `xorm_store.go` and is a maintainability concern (helper could take table + condition), but it does not constitute a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — Meaningless names `x, y` for deleteByIDs' (affected, err) results hurt readability, and the pattern is repeated at 556 and 578.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show assignments like `x, y := r.deleteByIDs(...)` followed by logging and returning those values (e.g., in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`). While `x` and `y` are arguably less readable than `affected` and `err`, this is a naming/style readability nit rather than a defect or substantial review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — The `"err", err` log field is always nil because the non-nil case already returned at line 532, so it is a dead field (same at 554 and 576).

adjudication.rationale: In the new callbacks, `err` is checked and returned on non-nil (`if err != nil { return 0, err }`) before the subsequent `r.log.Error(..., "err", err)`, so the logged `err` value will indeed always be `nil` at those points. However, this is just a minor logging nit (a redundant field), not a verifiable correctness/security defect or substantial review issue by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:584 — fetchIDs takes a raw SQL `condition` string that actually carries ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET clauses, so the name is misleading and the API is stringly typed (callers at 529, 549, 571).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `fetchIDs(ctx, table, condition string)` (new at ~571+) builds SQL as `SELECT id FROM <table> WHERE <condition>`, but callers pass strings that include `ORDER BY` and dialect `Limit/LimitOffset` fragments (e.g., `cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s AND created < %v ORDER BY id DESC %s`, ...)` and similar for max-count and orphan-tag cleanup). So the parameter is not just a WHERE condition; it’s effectively a full clause tail, making the API stringly-typed and the name/contract misleading. This is a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a directly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:585 — fetchIDs builds the SQL string before checking for an empty condition; the guard should come first so the reader is not misled.

adjudication.rationale: In fetchIDs, the function does initialize `sql := fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT id FROM %s`, table)` before checking `if condition == ""`, but this has no behavioral impact because the function returns immediately on empty condition and never uses the partially built SQL. The finding is purely a style/readability nit (order of statements), not a verifiable defect or substantial review issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:605 — Magic constant 999 and its "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" comment only describe SQLite before 3.32, while the new test targets the 32767 limit of newer versions, so comment and test disagree.

adjudication.rationale: In deleteByIDs(), the code hard-codes `const sqliteParameterLimit = 999` with a comment stating “SQLite has a parameter limit of 999” and uses that to decide when to inline IDs. The new test case sets `annotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767` and is titled as if it is validating SQLite >= 3.32.0’s higher variable limit (32767), but the implementation will inline IDs for any batch size > 999 regardless of SQLite version. So the test name/intent and the comment don’t align with what the code actually does, but this mismatch is not a functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The generic deleteByIDs helper picks its inline-vs-placeholder branch from annotation-specific r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize instead of len(ids), which couples it to cleanup config rather than the actual parameter count.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite parameter-limit decision is based on `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` rather than the actual number of IDs (`len(ids)`). This is a real coupling/maintainability issue in a generic helper: if `deleteByIDs` is ever called with an `ids` slice whose size doesn’t correspond to the cleanup batch size, the branch could be wrong. In the current diff’s call sites, `ids` are fetched with a `LIMIT(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize)`, so `len(ids)` will not exceed the batch size and this won’t manifest as a runtime defect today; it’s still a concrete review concern grounded in the new helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — The IN-list is built by repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation (quadratic, hard to read) where strings.Join over formatted ids would be clearer.

adjudication.rationale: In deleteByIDs(), when on SQLite with a batch size > 999, the code builds the IN-list string via repeated re-assignment using fmt.Sprintf in a loop: `values := fmt.Sprint(ids[0]); for _, v := range ids[1:] { values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) }`. This is verifiably quadratic-time string building and hurts readability; using a builder/strings.Join over preformatted ids would be clearer and more efficient. It’s not a correctness bug, but it can matter with the newly introduced very large batch sizes (e.g., 32767 in the new integration test).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:13 — The storage layer now imports sqlstore/migrator just to compare DB type, adding a dependency on the migration package for a dialect check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new import of `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/services/sqlstore/migrator` in `pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go` and it is used only for `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite` inside `deleteByIDs`. This introduces a dependency from the annotations storage layer onto the migrator package solely to identify SQLite, which is an architecture/dependency concern rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:274 — The batched InsertMulti loop (batchsize := 500) is duplicated verbatim for annotations and annotation tags (274 and 284), so it should be a small generic helper or shared constant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two very similar `InsertMulti` batching loops in `createTestAnnotations` (one for `newAnnotations`, one for `newAnnotationTags`) each with `batchsize := 500`. However, the finding is a DRY/refactoring suggestion in a test helper, not a defect or a substantive review issue introduced by the change (it doesn’t affect correctness/behavior). Under the rubric, this is a style/nit-level comment rather than an important non-bug issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cutting the ticker from 10m to 1m makes all eight cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history, tmp files) run 10x as often on every install, and because the 9m per-run timeout is unchanged, a heavy run can now go straight into the next one with no idle gap, so DB load never lets up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the cleanup loop ticker interval from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` -> `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)` in `pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral change that will make whatever cleanup work is performed in that loop run 10x as frequently, which can plausibly increase DB/system load. However, the finding’s specifics about “all eight cleanup jobs” and an unchanged “9m per-run timeout” are not verifiable from the provided diff, so it’s not a strictly provable defect from this patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Leftover debug logging at Error level writes the full `ids` slice (up to batch-size elements) plus two lines per batch at 534/537, 554/557, 576/579, including the final empty batch, so every cleanup run floods logs and allocates large formatted strings, now once a minute.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple unconditional `r.log.Error(...)` calls in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` that include the full `ids` slice (`"ids", ids`) and run once per batch: time-based cleanup logs at ~529 and ~533, count-based at ~551 and ~555, tags at ~573 and ~577. Because these logs are at Error level and occur even when `err` is nil, they will spam logs and potentially allocate/serialize large slices (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`). The loop also performs one final batch where `ids` is empty (fetchIDs returns empty; deleteByIDs returns 0), yet still emits the two log lines for that empty batch. The claim that this happens "now once a minute" is only indirectly suggested by `cleanup.go` changing its ticker to 1 minute; the diff doesn’t explicitly show annotation cleanup being scheduled there, but the logging issue itself is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — The SQLite IN-list is built by repeated `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`, which copies the whole string on every append and is O(n^2) (about 32k IDs means gigabytes of copying per batch); use strings.Builder or strings.Join.

adjudication.rationale: In deleteByIDs(), the SQLite branch builds the IN-list string by repeatedly doing `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop over `ids`. This re-copies the entire accumulated string each iteration (O(n^2)). With the newly supported large batch sizes (e.g., test sets 32767), this can lead to multi-GB transient copying and potentially severe slowdown or OOM during cleanup, i.e., broken runtime behavior under the conditions the diff explicitly adds support for.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — Each batch now takes two separate sessions and round-trips (SELECT ids, then DELETE ... IN (...)) instead of one statement, which doubles per-batch latency and connection churn at the default small batch size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes cleanup batching from a single DELETE statement per batch to a two-step process: `fetchIDs()` runs `r.db.WithDbSession(... session.SQL(...).Find(&ids))` to SELECT IDs, then `deleteByIDs()` runs another `r.db.WithDbSession(... session.Exec(...))` to DELETE those IDs. This is two DB sessions/round-trips per batch (in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`), which can increase per-batch latency/connection churn at small batch sizes. This is a performance/efficiency concern, not a correctness defect, and it is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug logging left at Error level (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579) fires on every batch, including successful and empty terminal batches with err=nil, so every instance emits error logs every cycle, which floods logs and trips error-rate alerts.

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go the new cleanup logic adds multiple unconditional `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the batch callbacks for MaxAge/MaxCount/tag cleanup (e.g., "Annotations to clean by time/count", "cleaned annotations", "Tags to clean", "cleaned tags"). These execute even when `err == nil` and even when `ids` is empty (terminal batch), because the logging happens before any `len(ids)==0` early return and passes `"err", err` regardless. This will generate error-level logs on every cleanup batch/cycle in normal operation and can flood logs / trigger error-rate alerts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:554 — Per-batch log lines include the full `ids` slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries, e.g. 32767), producing unbounded log lines that can exceed log shipper limits and bloat storage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds several per-batch `r.log.Error(...)` statements in `xorm_store.go` that include the full `ids` slice as a structured field (e.g., `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)`, similarly for "by count" and tag cleanup). Since `ids` is populated from `fetchIDs(...)` with a `LIMIT(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize)`, this can log up to the batch size worth of IDs (the test adds a 32767 batch-size case). This is a concrete, diff-grounded operational concern (very large log entries / storage/shipper limits), but it does not directly break correctness of the cleanup logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Ticker cut from 10m to 1m while the per-run timeout stays 9m (line 89), so with any backlog cleanup runs back-to-back nearly nonstop, and all eight jobs run 10x more often on every HA instance (clean() takes no server lock), which adds DB load and the delete contention this PR is meant to reduce.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go clearly changes the cleanup loop ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` -> `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`), which will make the cleanup jobs run 10x more frequently on every instance. While the finding’s claims about a 9m per-run timeout and HA locking are not verifiable from the provided diff snippet, the increased scheduling frequency and potential for increased load/contention is a concrete, diff-grounded operational concern rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — The non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so on MySQL/Postgres a configured batch size above 65535 makes every delete fail, and cleanup errors out permanently, where the old single-statement DELETE had no parameter limit.

adjudication.rationale: In the new implementation, `deleteByIDs` builds `DELETE ... WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` with one bound parameter per ID for non-SQLite DBs (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`), where `len(ids)` is bounded by `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` via `fetchIDs(... Limit(...))`. There is no guard for MySQL/Postgres parameter-count limits; if `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured very large, the statement can exceed driver/DB limits and return an error, causing `untilDoneOrCancelled` to stop and `CleanAnnotations`/cleanup to fail. The previous single-statement DELETE did not bind per-ID parameters, so this failure mode is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:610 — The SQLite inline-ID path builds the IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is O(n^2) (several GB of copying at 32767 IDs per batch) and can burn CPU and use up the cleanup timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite branch for `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` builds the `IN (...)` list by repeatedly reassigning `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. That pattern repeatedly copies the growing string, making it O(n^2) work for large `ids` slices (e.g., the added test uses batch size 32767). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/scalability issue that could increase CPU/time substantially, but it’s not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered only after createTestAnnotations and the count asserts, so a failure there leaks rows into the shared DB and the fixed IDs 1..N then cause PK collisions in every later subtest.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, `fakeSQL := db.InitTestDB(t)` is created once and shared across all subtests. Inside each `t.Run`, the test calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` and then asserts counts *before* registering `t.Cleanup(...)` that deletes from `annotation`/`annotation_tag`. Since `createTestAnnotations` uses `require.NoError` (fatal) and the asserts can fail, an early failure will prevent the cleanup from being registered/executed, leaving rows in the shared DB. Additionally, `createTestAnnotations` now sets explicit `ID: int64(i+1)`, so leftover rows can cause primary-key collisions in later subtests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:277 — require.NoError is called inside the WithDbSession closures and the closures always return nil, so the outer require.NoError(err) checks at lines 281 and 291 can never fail.

adjudication.rationale: In createTestAnnotations, both WithDbSession closures do always `return nil` and use `require.NoError(t, err)` inside the loop, but that does not mean the outer `require.NoError(t, err)` after `store.WithDbSession(...)` “can never fail”: `WithDbSession` itself can still return an error (e.g., session/transaction setup/teardown/commit failures) even if the closure returns nil. So the finding’s claim that the outer checks can never fail is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Each subtest now seeds fresh data, so "running the max count delete again" no longer re-runs cleanup on already-cleaned state and only checks the exactly-at-MaxCount case.

adjudication.rationale: In the new table-driven `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each `t.Run` now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` and only cleans the DB in a per-subtest `t.Cleanup`, so subtests no longer share state. The case named "running the max count delete again..." is no longer actually a second run on already-cleaned data; it freshly seeds `createAnnotationsNum: 9` and then expects `affectedAnnotations: 0` with `MaxCount: 3`, which contradicts the cleanup logic (a first run should delete 6). This makes the test case logically incorrect and likely failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:98 — The test name cites SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766), but the code switches at 999 (xorm_store.go:607), and no case tests batch size 999 or 1000, so a wrong threshold below 32767 would go unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The added integration test case is named "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER..." and uses batch size 32767, but the new SQLite-specific logic in deleteByIDs hardcodes a switch at sqliteParameterLimit = 999 (xorm_store.go) to avoid parameter limits. The test therefore doesn’t actually validate behavior around the implemented threshold (e.g., 999 vs 1000), and the name/intent mismatches the code path being exercised; this is a concrete test/clarity gap rather than a correctness bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:99 — The 40003-row case inserts about 120k rows and runs the O(n^2) fmt.Sprintf ID-string build in the SQLite path, which makes the suite much slower for one branch check.

adjudication.rationale: The new integration test case creates 40,003 annotations and 80,006 annotation_tag rows (≈120k inserts) via `createTestAnnotations(..., 40003, 0)` and then runs cleanup with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767`. In `xorm_store.go`, `deleteByIDs` has a SQLite-specific branch when `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` that builds the `IN (...)` list by repeatedly doing `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop over all IDs, which is quadratic-time string building and will be very slow for ~32k IDs. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/test-suite concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:643 — The new untilDoneOrCancelled, fetchIDs and deleteByIDs helpers have no tests for context cancellation (partial count plus ctx.Err), an error mid-batch, or the empty-condition guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new control-flow and safety logic in `untilDoneOrCancelled` (returns partial `totalAffected` plus `ctx.Err()` on cancellation), `fetchIDs` (explicit error when `condition == ""`), and `deleteByIDs` (early return on empty `ids`, plus SQLite parameter-limit branch). The updated `cleanup_test.go` exercises cleanup outcomes, but does not add targeted tests for these new edge cases (context cancellation behavior, error returned from `batchWork` mid-loop, or the empty-condition guard in `fetchIDs`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:569 — The rewritten orphaned-tag cleanup is only tested with tags orphaned in the same run (tags always equal 2x annotations), never with pre-existing orphans or a mixed state.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, `createTestAnnotations` always creates exactly two `annotation_tag` rows per annotation (`newAnnotationTags = ... TagID: 1, 2`), and the assertions in `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp` effectively tie orphan-tag deletions to annotation deletions (`assert.Equal(t, test.affectedAnnotations*2, affectedAnnotationTags)`). The test setup also deletes both `annotation` and `annotation_tag` in cleanup, so it never leaves behind pre-existing orphans. Given the rewrite of `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` to a new ID-fetch + `deleteByIDs` loop, there is no diff-visible coverage of scenarios with pre-existing orphan tags or mixed orphan/non-orphan states, which is a concrete missing edge-case test for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — The ticker drops from 10m to 1m with no test, and the 9m per-run timeout is now longer than the tick interval.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the ticker interval from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` -> `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`), which is a significant behavior/performance change to how often cleanup runs. The finding’s additional claim about a “9m per-run timeout” being longer than the tick interval is not verifiable from the provided diff (no timeout shown here), so only the tick-frequency concern is grounded.
